page: Amazon Web Services m7g.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton3 processor family. It features 48 physical ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 cores running at 2.6 GHz with a dedicated CPU allocation and no hyperthreading, providing one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present on this hardware configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves a strong rating in multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Memory bandwidth tests show strong throughput, reaching 4652.22 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 252.61 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic operations are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, though other extended instruction sets like AVX and AMX are absent due to the ARM64 architecture.

While multi-threaded execution, software compilation, and database operations like Redis SET demonstrate strong performance, single-core benchmarks remain in the average tier. Additionally, LLM text generation performance varies, showing weak results for small models but strong throughput for medium-sized models. Given the balanced resource allocation and high memory bandwidth, this instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations.

This instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, Redis databases, and static web serving, offering a cost-efficient profile for ARM-native deployments.
